speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you please describe the specific involuntary movements you are experiencing and when they first started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned a new onset movement disorder; can you describe the specific type of involuntary movements you are experiencing? Are they muscle stiffness, restlessness, or rhythmic jerking?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: This presentation of inner restlessness and the inability to remain still is highly suggestive of akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. To confirm this diagnosis, I need to know if these movements worsen when you try to sit or stand still, and if they bring you significant psychological distress or anxiety.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of starting risperidone two months ago and the specific symptoms of inner restlessness and pacing, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Risperidone-induced akathisia
